reason: I want to build the absorbing surface first; the picture shows the thin lining covering the fingerlike folds.
expectation: I expect a lined, folded intestinal surface that can help absorb food molecules.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and vein also have a clear connection, but I chose the absorbing surface first.

effect: The lining now covers the villi, and the comparison shows how folds provide more surface. I still need a nearby blood route.
reaction: The flattened comparison makes the purpose of the folds clearer.
reason: I’ll connect the capillaries to the liver-bound vein to build the blood side named in the goal.
expectation: I expect a connected blood route from the intestinal capillaries toward the liver, though it may still need to be joined to the lining.

alternatives.reason: Putting capillaries next to the lining also fits the new goal, but I want to complete the blood route first.

effect: The capillaries now connect to the vein leading to the liver, completing the blood side.
reaction: The route from small vessels to the larger vein makes sense.
reason: The only combination brings the absorbing lining close to the blood route, as the remaining goal asks.
expectation: I expect food molecules to cross the thin lining into nearby capillaries and travel toward the liver.

effect: The completed cutaway shows glucose and amino acids crossing the lining and tissue fluid into capillaries, then traveling toward the liver. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: Seeing the whole route come together was satisfying, especially because the molecules kept the same shapes.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the lining to the blood route was most worthwhile: it connected the folds, short crossing and transport to the liver in one picture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the capillaries to the vein was clear but less interesting on its own; it mostly prepared a route for the final join.

surprise.text: The flattened comparison made it clearer how the villi fit more surface into the intestine.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: both projects had clear goals, though the last combination was the only offered action.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter. Building separate parts and then seeing how they work together was satisfying, although the last choice was automatic in practice.
